transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?

It's my right knee — it's been aching on and off for about three years, but it's got noticeably worse over the last couple of months. It's getting in the way of things now, so I thought I'd better get it looked at.
How is your knee affecting your daily life at the moment, and do you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
I can't walk the dog round the park anymore, and I have to go down the stairs one step at a time holding the rail. As for medicines, penicillin gives me a rash.

Thanks for that. Could you tell me a bit about any other medicines you take — either regularly or that you've started or changed recently — and also any other health problems, illnesses or operations you've had in the past?

I take metformin 1 g twice daily, aspirin 75 mg once daily, atorvastatin 40 mg at night, and ramipril 5 mg once daily. As for other problems, I've had type 2 diabetes for about ten years, and six years ago I had a stent put in a heart artery.
How bad is the aching in your right knee these days — would you say it’s mild, moderate, or severe, or are you not sure?
On bad days it's about a 7 out of 10. It's bad enough that I can't walk the dog round the park anymore.
Have you noticed anything else going on with your right knee, besides the aching?
Yes, it sometimes swells up slightly by the evening. There's no redness, no fever, and it doesn't lock up on me.
Is there anything that seems to make the aching in your right knee better or worse?
It's worse going down stairs, and after I've been walking more than about 10 minutes. It's better if I rest it or take paracetamol.

You've already mentioned your diabetes and the heart stent — is there anything else about your past health, like other ongoing conditions, past illnesses, operations, or hospital stays, that you'd like to add?
No, that's the lot really — just the diabetes and the stent, nothing else I can think of.
Are there any other medicines you take, including anything new or changed recently?
No, nothing new or changed recently — those four are all I take.
Is there anything else you've noticed about your knee, or any other symptoms that came with it, that you'd like to add?
It does feel stiff in the morning for about 20 minutes or so. And the pain is a deep, grinding sort of ache on the inner side of the knee — it doesn't spread down the leg.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
